NOVA 2.5 keeps the original cyan cyber/neural-terminal interface and adds a secure Node.js API layer. It is a browser-based assistant, not a native Android system assistant.
- Original NOVA neural-core interface and toolkit layout
- Gemini chat through a Node.js server (the API key is not placed in browser code)
- Image attachments and camera capture for visual questions
- One-shot, user-started speech recognition and spoken replies where the browser supports them
- Gemini image generation endpoint and image-generator tool
- Android app launcher for selected apps using Android intent links, with web fallbacks
- Web search shortcut, YouTube, weather, currency conversion, translator, calculator, timer, notes, calendar, PDF opening, local audio playback, and other existing toolkit utilities
- PWA install metadata and basic offline shell caching
- A Gemini API key with access to the selected models
- Internet access for Gemini and online tools
2. Install Node.js 20+ if it is not already installed.
3. Open a terminal in the `NOVA_2.5` folder.
6. Open `.env` and replace the placeholder with your private Gemini API key.
Do not share your `.env` file or commit it to GitHub. `.gitignore` excludes it.

The app launcher tries Android intent URLs for selected apps such as YouTube, WhatsApp, Chrome, Maps, Gmail, Calendar, Drive, and Settings. Android/browser behavior varies by device. If an intent is unsupported, use the web fallback or open the app manually. A browser app cannot arbitrarily control other installed apps or silently access the phone.

Voice input starts only after the user taps the microphone. It is a short browser speech-recognition session, not always-on listening or Gemini Live. Camera and microphone permissions are requested by the browser. On hosted deployments, use HTTPS for camera/microphone access. Localhost is treated as a secure context by modern browsers.
This is a standard Node.js/Express project and can run on any host that supports Node.js 20 and environment variables (for example, a Node application host or your own server).
- Set environment variables on the host: `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_CHAT_MODEL`, `GEMINI_IMAGE_MODEL`, and optionally `PORT`.
- Do not upload `.env` or expose the Gemini key in frontend code.
- NOVA 2.5 is a web app. It cannot fully replace Gemini's native Android assistant, continuously listen in the background, or control every app.
- App launching depends on Android intent support and the app being installed.
- Browser timers, reminders, and local storage are not guaranteed to run or notify when the page is closed.

- Phone calls, contacts, background automation, and broad cross-app control are not included in this release. These are candidates for a later native Android/automation-focused NOVA 3.0, with explicit permissions and confirmations.
- Gemini usage may incur charges or be subject to account quotas. Image generation requires a model that supports image output.
- `GET /api/health` — checks server/API-key configuration (does not reveal the key)
- `POST /api/image` — generates an image using the configured Gemini image model

This package also includes Vercel serverless API routes (`api/chat.js`, `api/image.js`, and `api/health.js`) and root-level static files. You can deploy it through a GitHub repository without running the local Node server.
